**Observations from test image:**
- Very young soybean seedling, completely wilted and collapsed at the soil line
- Cotyledons and early leaves are yellowed/brown and drooping
- Plant is falling over — classic "damping-off" collapse pattern
- Sandy soil, early seedling stage

**Analysis:**
The collapse at the soil line with wilted, drooping leaves is the hallmark of post-emergence damping-off. Pythium causes water-soaked lesions on the hypocotyl that become soft brown rot, causing the seedling to fall over. The plant is clearly at a very early VE/V1 stage and has completely collapsed — consistent with Pythium_damping_off.

The Pythium reference images show pre-emergence seed rot, but the class encompasses both pre- and post-emergence phases. The other candidates (Rhizoctonia, Phytophthora) typically show distinct brownish stem lesions or affect more mature plants. This sandy soil with a collapsed early seedling fits Pythium best.
